# National Grid, Greater Worcester Community Foundation Award $250,000 to Support Home Weatherization Across Central Massachusetts


- [Home](https://www.nationalgrid.com/us/ny)
- [News](https://www.nationalgrid.com/news)


19th November 2026


*News*


#### *Funding will help households access weatherization improvements that can reduce energy use and lower bills*


WALTHAM, MA – National Grid and the National Grid Foundation, in partnership with[Greater Worcester Community Foundation (GWCF)](https://greaterworcester.org/) , announced $250,000 in awards to three Central Massachusetts nonprofits to help income-eligible households access weatherization improvements that can reduce energy use and lower their bills. The funding is part of National Grid’s[$5 million statewide energy-affordability initiative](https://www.nationalgrid.com/news/national-grid-and-foundation-announce-5-million-commitment-community-partners-energy-affordability) announced in January 2026. The grants will support critical weatherization improvements, lowering energy bills, and improving comfort for residents across Worcester County.


The grants to[Worcester Community Action Council](https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwcac.net%2Fabout-wcac%2F&data=05%7C02%7CBrian.Noyes%40nationalgrid.com%7C887900158d5b47eeb68108df3398d859%7Cf98a6a5325f34212901cc7787fcd3495%7C0%7C0%7C639286404451807429%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=sA5rIcoebRbBNtq9fEMUph62ZrvqDFOU%2BaqtyIOwZLI%3D&reserved=0) ,[Making Opportunity Coun](https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.makingopportunitycount.org%2Fabout-us%2F&data=05%7C02%7CBrian.Noyes%40nationalgrid.com%7C887900158d5b47eeb68108df3398d859%7Cf98a6a5325f34212901cc7787fcd3495%7C0%7C0%7C639286404451831976%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=hK9bh%2BfrSigOBGAXwJh7nmPbqb3GXxWq9kapT6pui74%3D&reserved=0) t, and the[North Central Massachusetts Habitat for Humanity](https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fncmhabitat.org%2F&data=05%7C02%7CBrian.Noyes%40nationalgrid.com%7C887900158d5b47eeb68108df3398d859%7Cf98a6a5325f34212901cc7787fcd3495%7C0%7C0%7C639286404451848229%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Hp%2B7Wqu%2FLJDBZ6g%2BBNcCyz%2F62Dgu0UCWwtJ7dFjOEtQ%3D&reserved=0) will support 300 households in the region overcome barriers that have prevented them from accessing critical weatherization programs, such as those offered by the statewide[Mass Save®](https://www.masssave.com/) program. The grants will also expand access to weatherization services for households that do not qualify for no-cost assistance but still face barriers to making energy-efficiency improvements that can reduce energy use and lower costs.


“As heating season begins, these grants will help households address weatherization improvements that can reduce energy use and lower their bills,” **said Lisa Wieland, President of National Grid – New England** . “By partnering with trusted community organizations, we can help more residents overcome the home repair and financial barriers that too often put these energy-saving programs out of reach.”


"By working with trusted community organizations that have deep roots and strong relationships in the local neighborhoods, we can better understand the specific home energy improvements and assistance that will have the greatest impact,” **said Robert Simmons, Vice President, National Grid Social Impact & Community Engagement and Executive Director, National Grid Foundation** . “Together, we can provide more targeted support and connect families with additional resources and unlock sustainable solutions that improve energy efficiency, reduce household energy costs and create a path toward energy affordability.”


Funded by National Grid and the National Grid Foundation, the grant program was managed and run by GWCF, which identified non-profits in the region with existing home energy improvement work or experience with contracted vendors that offered these services.


"Energy affordability and housing stability go hand in hand," **said Pete Dunn, President & CEO of Greater Worcester Community Foundation** . "We are proud to partner with National Grid, the National Grid Foundation and local nonprofits to help residents overcome barriers to weatherization services that can lower household expenses and improve quality of life. This investment will have a lasting impact on families throughout Worcester County."


The three grantees will deploy funding to help address issues such as roof repairs, electrical deficiencies, ventilation problems, asbestos remediation, and mold removal. The program will also support households that exceed Mass Save income eligibility thresholds but still face barriers to making energy-saving home improvements.


The Worcester-area grants are part of a $5 million statewide commitment announced by National Grid and the National Grid Foundation in January 2026 to help Massachusetts residents manage energy costs and access efficiency programs. Other investments supported through the initiative include partnerships with local United Way organizations, the Senior Energy Affordability Program administered by United Way of Massachusetts Bay and the Good Neighbor Energy Fund operated by The Salvation Army.

**About National Grid Foundation**


National Grid Foundation was created to enhance the quality of life across its grant making territory. The Foundation’s ongoing challenge is to create opportunities for solutions to educational and environmental issues. Its objective is based on the principle that giving people the tools to build hope is an essential ingredient in the development of individuals, families, and communities. Since its inception in December of 1998, the Foundation has granted more than $43 million to local community organizations. For more information,[please visit our website](https://www.nationalgrid.com/national-grid-foundation) .


**About Greater Worcester Community Foundation**


Greater Worcester Community Foundation is central Massachusetts’ leading community foundation, employing its expertise and resources to address the region’s most urgent needs. Since 1975, it has worked in partnership with donors to build a $270 million endowment composed of more than 650 named charitable funds and award over $186 million in grants that have helped transform communities and build a strong and vibrant region. For more information on the Foundation’s programs and how to give, please visit[www.greaterworcester.org](https://greaterworcester.org/) .
